## Additional production occurrence

During parallel F17, F18, F29, and F31 documentation work at code base `ae4030bd4a920762e27971f59a7aafdc4fcc0026`, `rebar comment prosaic-radon-sardine` committed the F29 GREEN evidence locally but terminal push recovery failed. The remote rejected `HEAD -> tickets` because another session had advanced the ref. Rebar reported 17 unpushed local ticket commits and stated that the backlog grew. The command exited zero after adding the local comment, so the write was durable in the shared tracker clone but was not shared through `origin/tickets` as the concurrency contract requires.

F31 recorded the matching stale-reference failure and a successful serialized control on this bug. The existing controlled proof also produced parallel failures and zero serialized failures. This occurrence therefore belongs to the confirmed common-directory coordination defect. No duplicate bug was created.

## Signed close publication failure

The F18 close command for `immolated-holohedral-waterdogs` returned exit 0 with a signed transition from `in_progress` to `closed` at commit `7fee4acbfa570b834b2bc917ce5febbc3e1b7862`. During the same command, tracker publication failed three times after automatic recovery because `origin/tickets` advanced. The reported local backlog grew from 45 commits to 57 commits and then to 70 commits.

Each failure was a non-fast-forward rejection for `HEAD -> tickets`. The command stated that the events were committed locally and would publish on the next successful push. A serialized `git fetch origin` completed before this occurrence was appended. This occurrence shows that the transient ref race can affect a signed close after the gate passes, even when the command reports success.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## RCA + GREEN evidence (fix implemented)

### Confirmed mechanism (runtime-verified)
Reproduced the exact common-directory fetch race with a deterministic real-git control in `tests/unit/test_fetch_common_dir_coordination.py::test_uncoordinated_parallel_fetches_can_race_but_coordination_prevents_it`: N linked worktrees sharing ONE Git common dir fetch `+refs/heads/tickets:refs/remotes/origin/tickets` concurrently while origin advances. WITHOUT coordination this surfaces `cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/tickets': is at <new> but expected <old>` (git's ref compare-and-swap loser); WITH the common-dir lock it produces zero CAS across many rounds. Root cause: remote-tracking refs live in the SHARED common dir, but the sync fetch (`rebar._store.sync.reconverge`) took no cross-process fetch lock at all, and the snapshot fetch (`rebar._snapshot.git_fetch.fetch_origin`) locked only on the snapshot-store path — neither coordinates the other, and the per-worktree advisory git-op lock (`gitutil._store_git_op_lock`, bug 9305) is keyed on the per-worktree git dir and skips the fetch legs.

### Fix (two composed mechanisms, both entry points)
1. `gitutil.fetch_coordination_lock(repo_root)` — a BLOCKING cross-process flock keyed on the canonical Git common dir (`_resolve_common_git_dir`: follows `commondir` pointers + `realpath`, so linked worktrees and the symlinked tickets clone collapse to one identity). Dedicated fetch lock, NOT the ticket write lock, and the fetch still runs OUTSIDE `.ticket-write.lock` — a blocked remote cannot block a local writer.
2. Bounded retry of the CAS mismatch (`git_outcome.is_ref_cas_mismatch`, classified distinctly from a held `<name>.lock`) for the residual race with a NON-rebar git peer. Sync stays best-effort (exhausted → skip round, no raise); snapshot fails closed with one actionable exhausted-recovery error.

### Verification (worktree venv)
- RED-before-fix confirmed: with the retry disabled (`_FETCH_CAS_ATTEMPTS=1`) the sync convergence test fails (`1 >= 2`); with the fix it converges. Snapshot path likewise raised on the first CAS pre-fix, now retries.
- Deterministic seam-injected retry tests at BOTH entry points + real-git common-dir identity (AC3) + lock mutual-exclusion + parallel coordinated control (zero CAS). 9 new tests pass; stable across 4 repeats (~20s).
- `make lint` PASS, `make typecheck` PASS (645 files), complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0. Affected suites (sync/snapshot/git_outcome, 140+ tests) green.
- docs/concurrency.md gains a 'Fetch coordination — the Git common-directory lock' subsection (AC7).

### Attribution
Per this ticket's Attribution section, the first-introducing commit `c5d79b58b6e829b336684c46cfc482c17c111c7a` has no recoverable ticket; attribution is pre-ticket and no `caused_by` edge is asserted. Layered on current origin/main (tip `cf7c31bec4b6`, after Gerrit 2178/2180), a distinct concern from their broad-fetch scoping.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

Parallel rebar operations can run Git fetches against one Git common directory without common coordination. Three concurrent plan reviews failed before verdict with `cannot lock ref refs/remotes/origin/tickets` and the comparison `is at <new> but expected <old>`. The failure is present on `origin/main` commit `3d41015574baa18a6ee6a25c7271be87fde1a3a5`. The authoritative concurrency contract in `docs/concurrency.md` lines 3 through 12 states that rebar is operated concurrently across interfaces and that every invariant gates every change.

## Duplicate sweep

Searches for the exact failure and for concurrent fetch coordination found no open or in-progress bug with this scope. `chordal-quasilegal-pipit` records the same failure during four concurrent reviews, but its accepted scope addressed plan-review verdict convergence. `icicled-unstable-urial` handles local Git contention on routed write calls. `honest-repulsive-blackfish` consolidates Git failure classification while preserving each caller action. `eclectic-spotted-barb` fixes an unlocked enrichment prune. None fixes this fetch race.

## Confirmed mechanism

`rebar._store.sync.reconverge` runs a forced-refspec fetch in `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` lines 281 through 295 before taking the store write lock at line 304. The snapshot fetch path serializes through a separate lock in the snapshot store. The store Git advisory lock introduced by `icicled-unstable-urial` covers routed index-mutating calls and explicitly leaves sync and push fetch legs outside its domain in `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` lines 300 through 307. Neither fetch path retries the stale-reference comparison failure.

Git fetch updates remote-tracking refs with compare-and-swap semantics. When two uncoordinated fetches update the same ref, one process can observe the ref after its peer changed it and fail with `is at <new> but expected <old>`. The snapshot path raises `SnapshotFetchError`, which aborts an attested operation. The sync path treats the fetch as a failed best-effort call and skips that freshness round.

## Proof

- A controlled experiment drove the production `sync._git` seam against fresh local repositories. Parallel execution produced 82 exact stale-reference comparison failures in 128 attempts. Serialized execution produced zero failures in 128 attempts.
- A second controlled experiment drove production snapshot fetches and production sync fetches against the same Git common directory. Nine of twelve snapshot fetches aborted with the exact comparison failure. Sync recorded 113 exact failures in 132 calls. The serialized control produced zero failures. This experiment proves that operation-specific locks do not coordinate paths that share refs. It does not assume that the standard code checkout and tracker clone share one object database.
- Fresh local repositories removed network behavior, credentials, missing objects, and ticket-store state as alternative explanations.
- Linked code worktrees share one Git common directory. Concurrent sessions also share the symlinked `.tickets-tracker` clone. Multiple operations can therefore update the same remote-tracking ref within either domain.

## Historical boundaries

Commit `c5d79b58b6e829b336684c46cfc482c17c111c7a` introduced tracker reconvergence with fetch deliberately outside the write lock. It predates the commit-trailer convention and has no recoverable ticket. Commit `57114212cf0112c43e571ded7cf8e16bc2a0e425` later ported that policy into `rebar._store` under `chilly-hyena-jet`. Commit `2a3abe6abde9` added the explicit destination refspec under `scorpioid-important-thylacine`. That refspec is required for narrow clones and must not be removed as a workaround.

`icicled-unstable-urial` records the operator decision that transient local Git contention should recover automatically and that only exhausted bounded recovery should surface an actionable error. Its accepted implementation was narrower than ref-updating fetches. `honest-repulsive-blackfish` provides shared failure vocabulary, but its acceptance criteria preserved existing caller actions and did not add fetch recovery. No attempted and reverted fix for this mechanism was found.

## Remediation constraints

- Coordinate rebar fetches by canonical Git common-directory identity, or apply bounded retry that safely re-reads state after the exact stale-reference comparison failure. The design may combine both mechanisms.
- Do not hold the ticket write lock across network I/O. Preserve the existing requirement that a slow fetch cannot block local ticket writers.
- Preserve the explicit tickets refspec required by `scorpioid-important-thylacine`.
- Preserve the context-specific Git outcomes established by `honest-repulsive-blackfish`. A local ref race, a remote policy rejection, and a ref CAS mismatch remain different outcomes.
- Treat non-rebar Git processes as possible peers. An advisory lock alone cannot provide recovery when another Git client does not take it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Parallel tracker synchronization calls against one Git common directory complete without exposing or silently discarding the stale-reference comparison failure.
- [x] An attested snapshot fetch racing with another ref-updating fetch against the same Git common directory completes through bounded recovery or returns one actionable exhausted-recovery error.
- [x] Coordination identity follows symlinks and linked worktrees to the canonical Git common directory.
- [x] Network fetches do not hold the ticket write lock, and a blocked remote does not block local ticket writes.
- [x] The explicit tickets destination refspec remains in place and narrow-clone synchronization tests remain green.
- [x] Deterministic tests use local repositories, observe the failure before the fix, and exercise parallel and serialized controls at both affected entry points.
- [x] Current concurrency documentation names the ref-fetch coordination and recovery policy.
- [x] Focused tests, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the project test gate pass.

## Attribution

The first introducing commit is `c5d79b58b6e829b336684c46cfc482c17c111c7a`. Searches by full SHA, exact policy text, `WS3`, and `REMEDIATION_PROPOSAL.md` found no originating ticket. The later Tier D story is a carrier. The explicit-refspec ticket is a required correctness fix rather than the origin. Attribution is therefore recorded as pre-ticket and no `caused_by` edge is asserted.
